title: Namo Bharat RRTS Guide 2026: Routes, Stations, Timings, Fare & Complete Travel Guide
description: Complete Namo Bharat RRTS guide 2026: full route map, all stations, live fare chart, train timings and ticket booking steps for the Delhi-Meerut corridor.
body:
Delhi and Meerut are now closer than they have ever been. The Namo Bharat train, India's first Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS), connects Sarai Kale Khan in Delhi to Modipuram in Meerut in under 60 minutes on a journey that used to eat up half your day on the road. Since the full 82.15 km corridor became completely operational on 22 February 2026, lakhs of daily commuters, students, and weekend travellers have switched to this high-speed rail line.

This guide covers everything you need before you board your first Namo Bharat train: the complete route map, the full list of stations, timings for weekdays and Sundays, standard and premium fares, and a detailed station-to-station fare table from Sarai Kale Khan all the way to Modipuram. If you want live route planning, use the [MetroGuideIndia Namo Bharat route planner](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/) to check the fastest route between any two stations.

## What Is Namo Bharat Metro?

Namo Bharat is the brand name for India's Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS), built and owned by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation ([NCRTC](https://ncrtc.in/)). People often call it the "[Namo Bharat metro](https://metroguideindia.com/blog/difference-between-metro-and-rrts-complete-comparison-2026.html)," but it is technically not a city metro. It is a semi-high-speed regional rail system designed to connect cities within the National Capital Region, running at speeds up to 180 km/h with an operational speed of around 160 km/h, which makes it the fastest rapid transit train in India.

The trains were earlier branded RapidX before being renamed Namo Bharat when passenger services began in October 2023. Day to day operations and maintenance are handled by DB RRTS Operations India, a subsidiary of Germany's Deutsche Bahn, under a long-term contract with NCRTC.

Each six-coach Namo Bharat trainset can carry around 1,750 passengers and comes fully air-conditioned with 2x2 transverse seating, overhead luggage racks, Wi-Fi, CCTV, automatic platform screen doors, and a dedicated women's coach. One coach on every train is reserved as a Premium Coach with extra legroom and a quieter cabin, positioned as the first coach when travelling from Delhi towards Meerut and as the last coach on the return journey.

## Namo Bharat Route: Delhi to Meerut

The Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut corridor is the first Namo Bharat line in the country and currently the only one that is fully operational. It runs for 82.15 km, starting at Sarai Kale Khan in Delhi and ending at Modipuram in Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh, passing through Ghaziabad along the way.

The corridor opened in phases over several years before becoming fully functional:

- **October 2023**: Priority section between Sahibabad and Duhai Depot (17 km) opened first
- **March 2024**: Extension to [Modinagar North](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/modi-nagar-north.html)
- **August 2024**: Extension to [Meerut South](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/meerut-south.html)
- **January 2025**: Extension to New Ashok Nagar
- **22 February 2026**: Full corridor from Sarai Kale Khan to Modipuram opened to the public, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi dedicating the complete 82.15 km line to the nation from Shatabdi Nagar station

At Sarai Kale Khan, the RRTS connects with the Delhi Metro Pink Line, Indian Railways at Hazrat Nizamuddin, and the Delhi ISBT, making it a major interchange hub for the whole network. Along the route, there are further interchanges with the Delhi Metro Blue Line at New Ashok Nagar, both the Pink and Blue Lines at Anand Vihar, and the Red Line at Ghaziabad.

If you are travelling from areas like New Ashok Nagar, Anand Vihar, or Ghaziabad, check the [New Ashok Nagar RRTS station page](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/new-ashok-nagar.html) or the [Ghaziabad RRTS station page](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/ghaziabad.html) on MetroGuideIndia for local exit gates, parking, and last-mile connectivity before you plan your trip.

### Namo Bharat Route Map at a Glance

Here is the sequence of stations from Delhi to Meerut on the Namo Bharat route:

Sarai Kale Khan → New Ashok Nagar → Anand Vihar → Sahibabad → Ghaziabad → Guldhar → Duhai → Duhai Depot → Muradnagar → Modi Nagar South → Modi Nagar North → Meerut South → Shatabdi Nagar → Begumpul → Modipuram

For an interactive version of this map with live route search between any two points, use the [Namo Bharat route planner on MetroGuideIndia](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/).

### Meerut Metro: The Local Extension Within Meerut

Alongside Namo Bharat, a separate local metro service called Meerut Metro (branded as India's fastest local metro at up to 120 km/h) runs on a 23 km stretch within Meerut city, sharing tracks and infrastructure with the RRTS. Four stations, Meerut South, Shatabdi Nagar, Begumpul, and Modipuram, are shared between both networks, while additional Meerut Metro-only stations include Partapur, Rithani, Brahmapuri, Meerut Central, Bhaisali, and MES Colony. If your journey ends inside Meerut city rather than at a shared RRTS station, you may need to switch to a Meerut Metro train, which you can do on the same platform at these interchange stations. Explore [Meerut Metro-specific stations like Partapur](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/partapur.html) and [Rithani](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/rithani.html) for more local details.

## Namo Bharat Timings 2026

Knowing the first and last train timings is important if you are planning an early morning office commute or a late return trip. Timings differ slightly between weekdays (Monday to Saturday) and Sundays.

| Direction | Monday to Saturday | Sunday |
| Delhi to Meerut (First Train from Sarai Kale Khan) | 06:00 AM | 08:00 AM |
| Delhi to Meerut (Last Train) | Around 10:30 PM | Around 10:00 PM |
| Meerut to Delhi (First Train from Meerut South) | 05:30 AM to 06:00 AM | 08:00 AM |
| Meerut to Delhi (Last Train) | Around 10:00 PM | Around 09:30 PM |

**Train frequency:** Namo Bharat trains run roughly every 10 minutes through most of the day. During peak office hours, frequency can tighten to every 5 to 8 minutes to handle the rush, while off-peak frequency may extend to every 12 to 15 minutes on some sections.

Since exact departure times can vary slightly station to station and are subject to periodic revision by NCRTC, always cross-check live timings using the [Namo Bharat first and last train timings page on MetroGuideIndia](https://metroguideindia.com/timings) before you leave home, especially for the very first or very last train of the day.

## Namo Bharat Fare 2026: Standard and Premium Coach Pricing

Namo Bharat fares are calculated on a distance-based model, meaning the farther you travel, the more you pay, but the per-kilometre rate reduces slightly on longer trips. There are two fare categories:

- **Standard Coach**: The regular travel class, priced from around ₹20 for the shortest hop up to about ₹210 for the full Sarai Kale Khan to Modipuram journey.
- **Premium Coach**: A single reserved coach per train with extra comfort and a quieter cabin, priced roughly 20 percent higher than Standard Coach, ranging from about ₹25 up to around ₹210 to ₹250 for the longest journey.

Fares can be paid using a Namo Bharat smart card, the Namo Bharat Connect mobile app (QR ticketing), or at station ticket counters and kiosks. The National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) is also accepted, allowing the same card to work across Namo Bharat, Delhi Metro, and several other transit systems under the "One Nation, One Card" initiative. Booking through the official app can offer a discount compared to walk-up ticket purchases, so it is worth downloading it before your first trip. Children below 90 cm in height generally travel free.

For the latest official rate card and any promotional discounts, check the [Namo Bharat fare guide on MetroGuideIndia](https://metroguideindia.com/fares).

## How Long Does the Full Journey Take?

The complete Sarai Kale Khan to Modipuram run covers 82.15 km in roughly 55 to 70 minutes, depending on the number of stops your train makes and time of day. That is a massive improvement over the 2.5 to 3 hour road journey between Delhi and Meerut during normal traffic, and can stretch to 4 hours or more during peak congestion on NH-58.

Some indicative travel times from Sarai Kale Khan:

- To Anand Vihar: around 8 to 10 minutes
- To Ghaziabad: around 15 to 18 minutes
- To Duhai Depot: around 22 to 25 minutes
- To Modi Nagar North: around 35 to 40 minutes
- To Meerut South: around 45 to 50 minutes
- To Modipuram: around 55 to 65 minutes

## Namo Bharat Delhi to Rishikesh: Is There a Direct Train?

A lot of travellers search for "Namo Bharat train Delhi to Rishikesh," hoping to combine an NCR commute with a trip to the Yoga Capital of the World. As of mid-2026, there is no operational Namo Bharat line to Rishikesh. The only fully running corridor is Delhi to Meerut.

That said, an extension is genuinely under discussion. Uttarakhand's government has proposed extending the Namo Bharat corridor beyond its current Modipuram terminus, running along the NH-58 alignment through towns like Daurala, Sakauti, Khatauli, and Purkazi near the UP–Uttarakhand border, then continuing to Roorkee, Haridwar, and finally Rishikesh. This proposal followed discussions between the Uttarakhand Chief Minister and the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister, and the state has sought funding for related infrastructure upgrades. However, this extension is still at the proposal and feasibility study stage, and no construction timeline or official inauguration date has been confirmed yet.

Until this extension is built, if you need to reach Rishikesh from Delhi, your fastest current options are the Vande Bharat or Shatabdi Express trains, or the recently completed Delhi–Dehradun Expressway by road, which brings travel time down to roughly 2.5 to 3 hours.

## Other Namo Bharat Routes in India: What Is Actually Planned

Several keyword searches ask about "Namo Bharat routes in India" beyond Delhi–Meerut, including mentions of Bihar and even an Ahmedabad to Bhuj line. Here is the honest picture: Namo Bharat is an NCR-specific project run by NCRTC, and there is currently no Namo Bharat corridor planned, under construction, or proposed in Bihar, nor is there any Namo Bharat line connecting Ahmedabad to Bhuj in Gujarat. Those routes are not part of the RRTS network.

What is genuinely part of the approved Namo Bharat Phase 1 plan, besides Delhi–Meerut, are two more corridors that will also converge at Sarai Kale Khan in Delhi, allowing cross-corridor travel without changing trains:

- **Delhi–Panipat–Karnal (Delhi–Sonepat–Panipat corridor)**: Around 196 km with roughly 22 main line stations, connecting Delhi to Sonepat, Gannaur, Samalkha, Panipat, and Karnal in Haryana.
- **Delhi–Gurugram–SNB (Delhi–Alwar corridor)**: Starting from Sarai Kale Khan and running through Munirka, Aerocity, Gurugram, Sotanala, and Rewari to Alwar in Rajasthan, benefiting industrial belts around Manesar, Bawal, and Neemrana.

Both of these corridors are in various stages of planning and construction and are not yet open for passenger service. Once operational, all three Phase 1 corridors will be interoperable through Sarai Kale Khan, meaning a single network will eventually connect Meerut, Panipat, and Alwar through Delhi.

## Namo Bharat Route from New Ashok Nagar

For commuters based around New Ashok Nagar in East Delhi, the RRTS station here connects directly to the Delhi Metro Blue Line, making it a convenient starting point if you live closer to Noida or East Delhi rather than central Delhi. From New Ashok Nagar, you can travel in either direction: towards Sarai Kale Khan and central Delhi, or towards Anand Vihar, Ghaziabad, and onward to Meerut. Fare from New Ashok Nagar to any station on the corridor is listed in the fare table above. For full local details including entry and exit gates and nearby connectivity, see the [New Ashok Nagar RRTS station page on MetroGuideIndia](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/new-ashok-nagar.html).

## Tips for a Smooth Namo Bharat Journey

- **Get a smart card or use the app.** Both save time at the gates and often come with small fare discounts compared to single-journey tokens bought at the counter.
- **Travel light during peak hours.** Anand Vihar, Sarai Kale Khan, and Ghaziabad see heavy footfall during the 8 to 10 AM and 6 to 8 PM windows.
- **Use the Premium Coach for longer trips.** If you are travelling the full stretch to Meerut, the extra comfort in the Premium Coach is worth the roughly 20 percent price bump.
- **Check interchange points in advance.** If your final stop is inside Meerut city rather than a shared RRTS-Meerut Metro station, plan your platform change at Meerut South, Shatabdi Nagar, Begumpul, or Modipuram.
- **Verify timings for the first and last train.** Sunday schedules start two hours later than weekdays, which catches many first-time riders off guard.
- **Cross-check fares before travelling.** NCRTC periodically revises fares, so treat the numbers in this guide as a close estimate and confirm the exact figure on the Namo Bharat Connect app.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Namo Bharat

#### **What is the full form of RRTS?** 

RRTS stands for Regional Rapid Transit System, the technical name for the network branded as Namo Bharat.

#### **Is Namo Bharat the same as Delhi Metro?** 

No. Namo Bharat is a separate regional rail system built by NCRTC for intercity travel within the National Capital Region, while Delhi Metro (DMRC) handles city-level transit within Delhi. The two networks interchange at stations like Sarai Kale Khan, New Ashok Nagar, Anand Vihar, and Ghaziabad, but Delhi [Metro and RRTS](https://metroguideindia.com/blog/difference-between-metro-and-rrts-complete-comparison-2026.html) are different.

#### **How many stations does Namo Bharat have on the Delhi–Meerut corridor?** 

There are 15 operational Namo Bharat stations between Sarai Kale Khan and Modipuram, plus additional Meerut Metro-only stations within Meerut city.

#### **What is the fastest speed of the Namo Bharat train?** 

Namo Bharat trains are designed for a maximum speed of 180 km/h, with an operational speed of around 160 km/h, making them the fastest rapid transit trains currently running in India.

#### **How much does a full Sarai Kale Khan to Modipuram ticket cost?** 

Around ₹210 for Standard Coach and roughly ₹250 for Premium Coach, based on current fare slabs, though you should confirm the exact fare on the day of travel.

#### **Is there a Namo Bharat train from Delhi to Rishikesh?** 

Not yet. An extension from Modipuram towards Roorkee, Haridwar, and Rishikesh has been proposed and discussed at the government level, but it remains in the feasibility and planning stage with no confirmed construction or opening date.

#### **Does Namo Bharat run on Sundays?** 

Yes, but with a later start. Sunday services typically begin around 8:00 AM instead of the usual 6:00 AM on weekdays.

#### **Can I use the same ticket for Namo Bharat and Meerut Metro?** 

Yes, at shared interchange stations like Meerut South, Shatabdi Nagar, Begumpul, and Modipuram, ticketing is integrated so you can move between the two services conveniently.
